candidates.explanation: The seeded admin gets its role straight from the seed. Admins created later get theirs from UsersService.create. The role handling there is elided in the snippet. It probably drops or overrides the requested role, or builds it with the wrong id or type. For example, it might hardcode the default user role, or look up the role in a way that never matches. A later admin would then be stored with a role the RolesGuard doesn't accept, and the guard would return 403. This is my best guess, because I couldn't see the elided code.

I haven't seen this file, so the line range and the defect are a guess. The controller applies `@Roles(RoleEnum.admin)` with `RolesGuard`. If the guard compares the role id with the wrong type or against the wrong value, only some admins would pass. An example is comparing a number to a string without `String()`, or comparing against a hardcoded user id. Super admin tokens could pass while later admins' tokens fail.

The seed is the only place that creates an admin with a correctly shaped role object. That is why the first account works and later ones don't. This is the least likely cause, because the seed itself looks correct.

fix.description: In UsersService.create, keep the role from the DTO. Check that its id is one of the RoleEnum values, comparing as strings, and assign it to the new user. Only fall back to the default user role when none is supplied. Also check that RolesGuard compares `String(request.user.role.id)` against the required roles mapped with `String`.
